cluster_summary: This cluster covers injection vulnerabilities (JDBC parameter injection, JNDI scheme injection, SQL injection) caused by incomplete blacklists, missing scheme or prefix validation, or direct string concatenation of user input into sensitive constructs. The majority of issues stem from assuming user-controlled data is safe when building JDBC URLs or SQL queries without proper validation, canonicalization, or parameterization.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled webhook URLs, callback URLs, endpoint parameters, or request destinations into outbound HTTP clients, URL.openConnection, fetch helpers, proxy clients, or webhook dispatchers. Report code paths where scheme, host, redirect target, DNS resolution, and private-address ranges are not constrained before the outbound request. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 9 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should enforce scheme and host allowlists, block private and metadata addresses after DNS resolution, and validate redirect targets.

mechanism.missing_guard: scheme, host, redirect target, DNS resolution, and private-address ranges are not constrained before the outbound request
mechanism.name: attacker-controlled webhook or callback URL fetch
mechanism.sink_shape: outbound HTTP clients, URL.openConnection, fetch helpers, proxy clients, or webhook dispatchers
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled webhook URLs, callback URLs, endpoint parameters, or request destinations
mechanism.typical_fix: enforce scheme and host allowlists, block private and metadata addresses after DNS resolution, and validate redirect targets

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Expand the blacklist to cover all known dangerous parameters and protocols, apply the check after full URL assembly and URL-decoding, and use robust regex that matches parameter names regardless of context.
sub_patterns.name: Incomplete or misapplied blacklist for JDBC connection parameters
sub_patterns.root_cause: The application relies on a blacklist to filter dangerous JDBC URL parameters, but the blacklist is missing entries (e.g., socketFactory, autoDeserialize, iiop), applied too early (before URL assembly or decoding), or uses overly restrictive regex patterns, allowing bypass.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Use parameterized queries (PreparedStatement) or, if necessary, apply strict allow-list validation or proper escaping.
sub_patterns.name: SQL injection via direct string concatenation
sub_patterns.root_cause: User-controlled input is concatenated into SQL query strings without parameterization, escaping, or allow-list validation, allowing injection of arbitrary SQL.

sub_patterns.name: Insufficient input validation in JDBC/JNDI URL construction and SQL query assembly
